items.name: Explore and Create: Artistic Creation
items.amount: Up to $75,000 per application, with at most 3 applications and $150,000 per calendar year. These figures come from the portal guidelines as summarised by several grant guides; canadacouncil.ca itself does not show an amount.
items.why_fit: This is the Council's main project grant and it now covers every stage from first idea to public presentation. In media arts only the director can apply, which is exactly Matthew's position on an independent, artist-driven Filipino-Canadian feature. It takes applications at any time, so he can apply now for the May to September 2027 shoot, and the budget can include the travel to Alberta and the Philippines.
items.priorities: Supports Canadian artists, groups and arts organizations to develop, create and share artistic works at any or all stages of the creative process, from initial idea to public presentation. Explore and Create encourages artists to investigate creative processes and take risks.
items.eligibility: Canadian artists (citizens or permanent residents) with a validated applicant profile in the Council's portal, plus artistic groups and arts organizations. For media arts (film, video, moving images) only the director or creator of the work may apply. Producers and production companies cannot apply on a project's behalf.
items.watch_out: Media arts requests 'must be for works that are independent of the commercial industries of film, television and video games', and the Council does not fund commercial film projects. Present PURPLE as an independent, artist-driven work, and ask a program officer before combining this grant with Telefilm money or a commercial distributor. Matthew first needs a validated profile (the 'Artist or arts worker' profile; validation takes up to 15 business days). With only an AD credit and no directing credit, he should check the profile's professional-practice criteria before applying. The application must be submitted before the project start date, and results take about 5 months. The $75,000 maximum and the question list could not be read on canadacouncil.ca, because the portal pages only load in a browser; confirm both in the portal's application preview. Grants are taxable income and are reported on a T4A.
items.deadline: Rolling: any time before the start date of your project or activity. Results usually come within 5 months of submitting, so apply by mid-December 2026 to hear back before the May 2027 shoot.
items.decision: Usually within 5 months of submitting your application.
items.how_to_apply: 1) Create a new account in the updated Canada Council portal. Accounts made before August 2025 must be re-created; history transfers if you use the same email. 2) Request the 'Artist or arts worker' applicant profile, with an arts CV showing how you meet its criteria; staff validate it in up to 15 business days. 3) Open the Artistic Creation funding opportunity and use the link to preview the application questions. 4) Prepare a project description, budget, timeline, arts CV and work samples (for example a clip from Quiet Father, a PURPLE pitch or lookbook video, and script pages). 5) Submit before the project start date; aim for mid-December 2026.
items.tips: Grant guides that summarise the portal guidelines say assessment weighs artistic merit most (about 50%), then impact (30%), then feasibility (20%), and that work samples carry a lot of weight. Set the project start date after the expected decision, about 5 months after you submit. A later stage, such as post-production, can be a separate application within the yearly cap. Artistic Creation replaces the former Research and Creation and Concept to Realization components, so older advice about those components may no longer apply.

items.name: Arts Across Canada and Abroad: Micro-grants
items.amount: Small grants for career development and travel. canadacouncil.ca shows no amount; grant guides report up to $10,000 per application.
items.why_fit: Micro-grants now cover what the Council's professional development and Arts Across Canada and Arts Abroad travel grants used to fund. Matthew could use one to attend a first-feature lab or market, or to travel with PURPLE to a festival that selects it in 2028.
items.priorities: Supports activities that support the professional growth and advancement of artistic careers or practices. Replaces Explore and Create: Professional Development for Artists, Supporting Artistic Practice: Professional Development for Arts Professionals, Arts Across Canada: Travel and Arts Abroad: Travel.
items.eligibility: Artists, arts workers, groups and organizations with a validated Canada Council applicant profile.
items.watch_out: The program is about career development and travel to share work. It is not described as covering production travel, so put the costs of shooting in Alberta and the Philippines in an Artistic Creation budget instead. The maximum amount and eligible costs are only in the portal (not confirmed on canadacouncil.ca). You need a validated profile, and the application must go in before the activity or departure date.
items.deadline: Rolling: any time before the start date of your project or activity, or your departure date. Results usually come within 4 months of submitting, so apply at least 4 months ahead.
items.decision: Usually within 4 months of submitting.
items.how_to_apply: Create a portal account and get the applicant profile validated (up to 15 business days). Open the Micro-grants funding opportunity, preview the questions, and submit at least 4 months before the activity or departure.

items.name: Arts Across Canada and Abroad: Representation and Promotion
items.amount: Travel costs. Amounts are set in the portal guidelines; none are shown on canadacouncil.ca.
items.why_fit: Once PURPLE is finished in 2028, this can pay for travel to promote it at markets or festivals abroad, for example screenings in the Philippines or at Asian festivals, to find distributors and audiences.
items.priorities: Funding for travel activities linked to promotion and the development of markets for artists and works from Canada.
items.eligibility: Artists and organizations from Canada with a validated applicant profile. The public page does not spell out applicant types; check the portal.
items.watch_out: This is only useful after the film is finished, so it does nothing for the production gap. Amounts, eligible costs and applicant types are only in the portal. Apply before departure; results take about 4 months.
items.deadline: Rolling: any time before your departure date. Results usually come within 4 months of submitting.
items.decision: Usually within 4 months of submitting.
items.how_to_apply: Through the Canada Council portal with a validated profile. Submit at least 4 months before the trip, with the invitation or market accreditation and a promotion plan.

items.name: Arts Across Canada and Abroad: Circulation and Touring
items.amount: Amounts are set in the portal guidelines; none are shown on canadacouncil.ca.
items.why_fit: A 2028 screening tour of the finished film along its own route (Toronto, Ottawa, Montreal, Alberta) with Filipino-Canadian and community presenters, with the director travelling to present it, could fit this touring support.
items.priorities: Supports the touring and circulation of Canadian artists, exhibitions and works, both nationally and internationally.
items.eligibility: Artists, artistic groups and arts organizations from Canada with a validated applicant profile.
items.watch_out: You need confirmed invitations from presenters or venues. Whether a screening tour of a feature film qualifies, and the amounts, are only in the portal guidelines, so confirm with the Council. 3 Feb 2027 is the next deadline overall but is too early, because the film won't be finished; use 9 Jun 2027 for screenings from about November 2027, or 6 Oct 2027 for screenings from about March 2028. Results take about 5 months after the deadline. This is release money, not production money.
items.deadline: Deadlines: 3 Feb 2027, 9 Jun 2027 and 6 Oct 2027 (the closing time is shown in the portal). For PURPLE's early-2028 screenings, the 9 Jun 2027 deadline is the realistic one.
items.decision: Usually within 5 months of the deadline.
items.reopens: Three deadlines a year; after 6 Oct 2027 the next ones are expected in early 2028.
items.how_to_apply: Through the Canada Council portal with a validated profile. Line up written invitations from presenters (community centres, festivals, cinemas) on the route before the deadline.

items.name: Talent to Watch: Filmmaker Apply-Direct Stream
items.amount: Non-repayable contribution that can cover up to 100% of the film's financing; maximum $250,000 for fiction features.
items.why_fit: This is Telefilm's first-feature program. Teams whose producers, writer and director all belong to listed groups, including People of Colour, can apply without a partner's recommendation, and the contribution can cover the whole of PURPLE's financing. Telefilm says it may prioritize teams from Black, Indigenous and People of Colour communities.
items.priorities: Discover and develop the next generation of Canadian filmmakers through a first feature; fund films with cultural impact and audience engagement; advance equity and representation (Indigenous, Black, People of Colour, 2SLGBTQIA+, gender-diverse, disability), creative teams outside the main production centres, and meaningful collaboration with the communities a film depicts.
items.eligibility: Producers, directors and screenwriters who are Canadian citizens or permanent residents and emerging: each has made at least a short (30 minutes or less), web, TV, commercial or music-video work, or has equivalent experience, and has not held the same key role on a feature of 75 minutes or more. In this stream every key creative must be Indigenous, Black, a Person of Colour, a woman, gender-diverse, 2SLGBTQIA+, a person with a disability or an OLMC member. An individual can apply on behalf of a company to be incorporated if the project is selected.
items.watch_out: PURPLE must run at least 75 minutes; a 65-page script may come in short. Budgets are expected to be between $150,000 and $500,000 (Telefilm 'may show flexibility'), so the $47,335 budget would need to be rebuilt to include E&O insurance, closed captions, described video and versions in both official languages. If selected, the team must incorporate a Canadian-controlled company that is wholly owned by the key creatives and owns 100% of the rights. The film needs 8 of 10 CAVCO points. Timing is the biggest issue: the intake is expected in April 2027, and decisions come about 80 business days after the close (around August 2027), which is after the planned May 2027 start. Completion projects are not eligible, so ask Telefilm before shooting anything. Every credited producer must belong to a listed group; otherwise use the Industry Partner Stream. A project can be submitted only once.
items.deadline: 2026-27 intake: opened 14 Apr 2026, 8:00am EDT; closed 28 Apr 2026, 11:59pm EDT. 2027-28 dates are not yet published.
items.decision: Telefilm aims to decide within 80 business days of the closing date for complete applications.
items.reopens: The last intake ran 14 to 28 April 2026; the next is expected in April 2027 (fiscal 2027-28).
items.closed_reason: 2026-27 intake closed 28 Apr 2026.
items.how_to_apply: 1) Open a Dialogue account and create an Organization for the company to be incorporated. 2) Prepare every required document; anything missing must be sent within 5 business days of Telefilm's notice. 3) Submit in Dialogue during the April window. 4) Every producer, writer and director receives a self-identification questionnaire after submission. 5) If selected: incorporate, join the INIS/NSI mentorship program, and start principal photography within 18 months of the decision letter.
items.tips: The creative assessment focuses on the pitch video, synopsis, director's vision and community engagement plan. Use the community plan to explain the Filipino-Canadian lived experience of the team, consultation with the community, work with the local Philippine crew, and why Tagalog dialogue is an artistic imperative. Reel Asian has offered consultations to Asian-identifying teams applying to the Direct Stream (programming@reelasian.com). Only recommended projects receive feedback, and a project gets one try unless Telefilm invites it to reapply, so don't submit early drafts.

questions.hint: The full, production-ready PURPLE screenplay. It is read only if the project is shortlisted, but it must be attached.

questions.q: Presentation video: working title; genre, type and length; key creative team and track records; synopsis from beginning to end; the team's vision and visual treatment; what sets the project apart; target audience; a 1-minute segment of the director's previous short
questions.limit: 5 minutes (link embedded in a Word document)
questions.hint: A pitch video covering every listed element, with only the team's own footage. Telefilm says to give it particular attention.

questions.q: Synopsis of the project, telling the story from beginning to end
Audience Engagement and Discoverability Plan (Telefilm form)
Track record for producer, screenwriter and director (Telefilm template, one per person)
Production schedule from pre-production to release, showing principal photography within 18 months of the decision letter

items.name: Talent to Watch: Industry Partner Stream
items.amount: Non-repayable contribution that can cover up to 100% of the film's financing; maximum $250,000 for fiction features.
items.why_fit: If any of PURPLE's credited producers is not in a listed group, a recommendation from a Designated Partner opens the same first-feature money. Toronto partners include Reel Asian, Reelworld Screen Institute, the Canadian Film Centre, TIFF, CaribbeanTales and the DGC, plus film schools (York, Toronto Metropolitan, Humber, Sheridan) whose recent graduates qualify.
items.priorities: Same as the program as a whole: first features by emerging Canadian teams with cultural impact and audience reach, with a priority on equity and representation. Partners are training institutions, film co-ops and festivals with talent incubators.
items.eligibility: Emerging producers, directors and screenwriters (same rules as other streams) whose project is recommended by a Designated Partner. Main component: the director must be a recent graduate (within the last 5 years) of the partner's production program, an active member (within the last 3 years) of its film co-op, or a participant in its festival incubator. Producers and writers do not need that link but must be emerging.
items.watch_out: Matthew needs a real link to a partner: someone who registers with the partner on or near the day they apply does not count as an active member. Each partner runs its own selection and sets its own deadline, earlier than Telefilm's (2026 examples: Whistler Film Festival 30 Mar, Yukon Film Society 20 Apr). All the program-wide issues also apply: a runtime of at least 75 minutes, an expected budget of $150,000 to $500,000, incorporation if selected, 8/10 CAVCO points, captions, described video and both official languages, and an August decision that lands after a May 2027 shoot start.
items.deadline: Telefilm's 2026-27 window ran 14 Apr 2026, 8:00am EDT to 28 Apr 2026, 11:59pm EDT. Partner recommendation deadlines come earlier (often March) and are set by each partner; 2027 dates are not yet published.
items.decision: Telefilm aims to decide within 80 business days of its closing date.
items.reopens: Partners usually call for projects in late winter, before Telefilm's April window; the next Telefilm window is expected in April 2027.
items.closed_reason: 2026-27 intake closed 28 Apr 2026.
items.how_to_apply: 1) Check which Designated Partner Matthew has a qualifying link to (see the 2026-27 partner list, which includes contacts such as Reel Asian aram@reelasian.com and Reelworld industry@reelworld.ca). 2) Apply to that partner's own selection process early in 2027. 3) If recommended, get the signed Letter of Recommendation (Telefilm template). 4) Apply in Dialogue during Telefilm's April window with all the required documents plus the letter.
items.tips: Partners must judge that a project is production-ready, feasible at its budget, and able to start principal photography within 18 months, so bring a finished script, budget and schedule. Partners may mentor or give in-kind help but cannot take rights or a share of Telefilm's money. Telefilm notes that the director should not also be the lead producer.

questions.q: Letter of Recommendation from the Designated Industry Partner (Telefilm template)
questions.hint: Signed by the partner; it confirms the director is a recent alumnus, an active member or an incubator participant.
Same pitch video as the Apply-Direct stream; see the required-documents list.

questions.q: Audience Engagement and Discoverability Plan (Telefilm form)
Track record for producer, screenwriter and director (template)

items.name: International Promotion Program: participation in international festivals
items.amount: For a feature, per festival: up to $25,000 (Category 1), $15,000 (Category 2), or $2,000 ($5,000 for a world or international premiere) (Category 3); up to $40,000 per feature in total. Travel to co-production markets for invited projects: $2,000 per person, $4,000 per event.
items.why_fit: If PURPLE is selected for a recognized international festival in 2028, Telefilm can pay the team's travel and publicity costs there. The program counts a film as a feature if the festival selects it as one, which helps a 65 to 75 minute film.
items.priorities: Promoting Canadian content and talent abroad through participation in international festivals, forums, co-production markets and Telefilm's international initiatives.
items.eligibility: The producer, distributor or sales agent of the film, which must be a Canadian-controlled company with its head office in Canada. The film must be a Canadian feature certified (or eligible) by CAVCO with 8 of 10 points and officially selected at a festival in the tiers listed in Appendix A.
items.watch_out: Needs a production company and an official selection at a listed festival (Appendix A is a separate document; other festivals are at Telefilm's discretion). Apply at least 3 weeks before the festival opens, while a window is open and funds remain. Costs already paid by the festival or another funder can't be claimed. It does nothing for the production gap.
items.deadline: Apply at least 3 weeks before the festival opens, within an open window. The 2026-27 window runs 14 Apr 2026, 8:00am EDT to 16 Feb 2027, 11:59pm EST, subject to available funds.
items.reopens: A new window is expected each April (2027-28 and 2028-29); PURPLE would use the window covering its 2028 festivals.
items.how_to_apply: In Dialogue, as the Canadian production company, with the festival's official selection letter and a budget of eligible costs, at least 3 weeks before the festival.

items.name: Marketing Program (Canada Feature Film Fund)
items.amount: Marketing and promotion: repayable advance of up to 75% of eligible Canadian marketing costs. Versioning (such as French subtitles): repayable advance of up to 75%, capped at $420 per minute to $48,000 for a theatrical release ($380 per minute to $43,200 for TV or digital). Audience-engagement activities: non-repayable, up to 100% of the activity.
items.why_fit: If PURPLE gets Talent to Watch money, this is the follow-on for its 2028 release. Telefilm gives priority to films it funded, and audience-engagement activities such as Filipino-Canadian community screenings can be funded non-repayably.
items.priorities: Increase awareness and audiences for Canadian films, including impact campaigns, hybrid, platform-based or festival-led releases, and marketing investment for films from equity-deserving communities.
items.eligibility: The Canadian production or distribution company of the film, Canadian-controlled with its head office in Canada and financially stable. The film must be a feature of at least 75 minutes with 8 of 10 CAVCO points. Priority goes to films funded by Telefilm's Production, Theatrical Documentary or Talent to Watch programs.
items.watch_out: Needs a company, a runtime of at least 75 minutes and 8/10 CAVCO points. It is realistic mainly if Telefilm already funded the production. Most support is a repayable advance, and costs must be for services in Canada. If a distributor is attached, a producer applying needs the distributor's written authorization. Apply before spending.
items.deadline: Within the yearly window, subject to funds. The 2026-27 window runs 23 Apr 2026, 8:00am EDT to 16 Feb 2027, 11:59pm EST.
items.reopens: A new window normally opens each spring; PURPLE would apply in the 2027-28 window ahead of its early-2028 release.
items.how_to_apply: In Dialogue, with a marketing or audience-engagement plan and budget, before the activities start.

items.name: Canadian Film or Video Production Tax Credit (CPTC)
items.funder: Canadian Audio-Visual Certification Office (CAVCO), Canadian Heritage, with the Canada Revenue Agency
items.amount: Fully refundable credit of 25% of qualified labour expenditure, with labour capped at 60% of production cost (net of assistance), so at most 15% of net production cost.
items.why_fit: PURPLE has a Canadian writer-director, so it can earn the key CAVCO points, and the credit refunds part of the Canadian crew and cast wages even with no broadcaster. It is also the certification Telefilm and Ontario's tax credit build on.
items.priorities: Encourage Canadian programming and develop an active domestic production sector by refunding part of the Canadian labour cost of certified Canadian productions.
items.eligibility: A prescribed taxable Canadian corporation that is Canadian-controlled and primarily carries on a Canadian film or video production business through a permanent establishment in Canada. The production needs at least 6 of 10 creative points (director 2, screenwriter 2, each of the two highest-paid lead performers 1, DOP 1, art director 1, composer 1, picture editor 1). The director or screenwriter, and one of the two highest-paid lead performers, must be Canadian, and all producers must be Canadian.
items.watch_out: It needs a production corporation that owns the copyright for 25 years. It also needs a written fair-market-value agreement with a Canadian distributor or a CRTC-licensed broadcaster (or an acceptable online service) to show PURPLE in Canada within two years of completion. At least 75% of producing-service costs must be paid to Canadians and 75% of post costs incurred in Canada, so the Philippine local crew counts against the 25% non-Canadian allowance. The credit is based on Canadian labour, so Philippine crew wages generally won't add to it. The cash only arrives after the corporation's tax return is assessed, so it can't fund the shoot unless it is bridged. Each certificate (Part A and Part B) costs 0.15% of the eligible production cost. Telefilm needs 8 points (not 6).
items.deadline: Rolling: no deadline for Part A. Part B is due within 24 months of the end of the corporation's first tax year ending after principal photography starts, extendable to 42 months with T2029 waivers filed with the CRA.
items.decision: CAVCO's service standard is 180 calendar days from a complete application to certification or denial.
items.how_to_apply: 1) Incorporate a Canadian-controlled production company before production and put the rights and contracts in its name. 2) Get CAVCO personnel numbers for key creatives. 3) Apply for the Part A certificate (eligibility) in CAVCO Online, ideally before or during production. 4) Secure a Canadian distributor or broadcaster agreement. 5) After completion, apply for the Part B certificate with audited costs. 6) Claim the credit on the company's T2 return with Form T1131.
items.tips: At PURPLE's $47,335 budget the ceiling is about $7,100 (15% of net cost), and only if Canadian labour is at least 60% of costs. Paying deferred or nominal fees reduces the credit, so book real wages to Canadian crew. The company structure should also suit Telefilm (wholly owned by the key creatives) and Ontario's OFTTC.

items.name: Canada Summer Jobs 2027
items.funder: Employment and Social Development Canada (Service Canada)
items.amount: Private-sector and public-sector employers: up to 50% of the provincial or territorial adult minimum hourly wage. Not-for-profit employers: up to 100% of it, plus mandatory employment-related costs.
items.why_fit: Jobs can run 6 to 16 weeks between 19 Apr and 28 Aug 2027, which covers PURPLE's May to July Ottawa, Montreal and Alberta shoot. The subsidy could pay part of the wages of youth production assistants or trainees aged 15 to 30.
items.priorities: Paid summer work experience for youth aged 15 to 30, with quality jobs, supervision and mentoring; applicants say whether each job supports national priorities and any local priorities set by the MP.
items.eligibility: Not-for-profit organizations, public-sector employers, and private-sector employers (incorporated or not, including partnerships and sole proprietorships) with 50 or fewer full-time employees. The employer needs its own CRA business number and must have operated for at least 2 years by 31 Dec 2026, unless it had CSJ 2026 funding. Youth must be 15 to 30, Canadian citizens, permanent residents or protected persons with a SIN; international students are not eligible.
items.watch_out: A newly formed production company will not meet the 2-year rule. The employer would have to be an existing sole proprietorship or company of Matthew's or a producer's, with its own business number and at least 2 years of operation, or a not-for-profit partner (which gets 100%). Private employers receive only 50% of minimum wage. Jobs must be full-time (30 to 40 hours a week) for 6 to 16 consecutive weeks. The deadline is only weeks away.
items.deadline: 3 Dec 2026, 11:59pm PT (the window opened 27 Oct 2026).
items.reopens: Next call (CSJ 2028) expected in autumn 2027.
items.how_to_apply: Apply online through Grants and Contributions Online Services (GCOS), or by mail or in person, by 3 Dec 2026. Have the CRA business number, health and safety, workers' compensation and anti-harassment details ready. Complete Part A (employer), Part B (one section per job) and Part C (funding), then sign the attestation.

questions.q: Part A: Employer information (organization details, business number, job location, health and safety, workers' compensation, anti-harassment and anti-discrimination practices)
questions.hint: Legal name and business number of the employer, and the safety and harassment policies for the set.

questions.q: Part B, Q27: Job details (job title, tasks, work arrangement, language, supervision, skills, mentoring, retention, recruitment, priorities)
questions.hint: For example 'Production assistant (youth)': on-set duties, who supervises, the skills learned, and how you will recruit, including youth from the Filipino-Canadian community.

questions.q: Part C: Funding (participants, dates, weeks, hours, wage, total funding requested)

items.name: Multiculturalism and Anti-Racism Program: Events component
items.amount: Up to $100,000 per event per fiscal year.
items.why_fit: A free public screening of PURPLE with a discussion on Filipino-Canadian family, grief and belonging, co-presented with a Filipino-Canadian community group, fits the program's support for events that celebrate a community's history and culture and build intercultural understanding.
items.priorities: Community-based events that promote intercultural or interfaith understanding, discussion of multiculturalism, diversity, racism and religious discrimination, or celebrate a community's history and culture (such as heritage months). Current priorities: community-led efforts to counter hate and misinformation, and gatherings that build human connection and belonging.
items.eligibility: Canadian not-for-profit organizations, associations and unincorporated groups; small municipalities (up to 10,000 people); Indigenous not-for-profits and governments. Events must be open to the general public.
items.watch_out: Individuals and for-profit companies cannot apply, so a not-for-profit or community partner (or an unincorporated not-for-profit group) must be the applicant. It pays event costs only (venue, artist and speaker fees, promotion, domestic travel, captioning and translation), not the film. Profit-making, commercial or private events, food and drink, international travel, and costs incurred before the application is received are ineligible. Financial statements and organizational documents are required. The online portal is down, so forms must be requested by email.
items.deadline: For events starting 1 Dec 2027 to 31 Mar 2028 (PURPLE's January 2028 screening): intake 12 May 2027, 8:00am ET to 22 Jun 2027, 4:00pm ET. The other 2027-28 intake runs 13 Jan to 24 Feb 2027, 4:00pm ET, for events from 1 Aug to 30 Nov 2027.
items.decision: Receipt is acknowledged within two weeks; the decision time is not stated.
items.how_to_apply: Email the Ontario regional office for the Application Form and Budget Form. Complete, sign and date them, attach the attestation, a balanced budget (Program template), recent financial statements and organizational documents, and email everything to the regional office during the intake.
items.tips: Applications are assessed on event design, goals and rationale (clear need, confirmed partners, positive interaction between communities), on results, budget integrity and value for money, and on capacity to deliver. Pair the screening with a panel or workshop, keep it free and public, and show confirmed partners.

items.name: CISF programs for BPOC creators (CISF Connect and future funds)
items.funder: Canadian Independent Screen Fund for BPOC Creators (CISF)
items.amount: No fiction-feature funding open. The 2026 Hot Docs-CISF Connect Audience Engagement Grant was a single $10,000 award for a documentary.
items.why_fit: CISF is the national, BPOC-governed fund for Black and racialized screen creators. Its CISF Connect audience initiative funds producer marketing and trains Film Engagement Specialists to run community screenings, which suits PURPLE's 2028 Filipino-Canadian screenings if CISF opens it to fiction.
items.priorities: Supports emerging, intermediate and experienced creators from BPOC communities in the development and production of screen projects, and Canadian-owned BPOC production companies. CISF Connect aims to build lasting audiences for films by Black and racialized filmmakers, beyond one-off festival premieres.
items.eligibility: Generally Canadian-owned BPOC production companies or productions. The 2026 CISF Connect grant required a Canadian documentary by a Black or racialized filmmaker that screened at Hot Docs 2026.
items.watch_out: No CISF program is currently open to a fiction feature. The 2026 CISF Connect grant was for documentaries (closed 31 May 2026), and the Rogers-BSO Script Development Fund is for TV series and documentaries and is closed. CISF was named among the funds receiving money in Budget 2026, so new programs may appear, but none are announced. CISF funding generally targets Canadian-owned BPOC production companies.
items.reopens: Watch independentfund.org and the CISF newsletter for programs funded through Budget 2026; no 2027 dates are published.
items.closed_reason: No open CISF program fits a fiction feature (checked 2026-11-16).
items.how_to_apply: Sign up for the CISF newsletter and use the contact form (independentfund.org/contact) to ask whether CISF Connect will accept fiction features in 2027-28.

items.name: Media Artists: Creation Projects (Emerging)
items.amount: Emerging: up to $10,000 (Mid-Career and Established: up to $40,000). You may ask for up to 100% of project costs; total project budget must not exceed $125,000 for Emerging.
items.why_fit: The main Ontario grant for a director's own independent film: drama is an eligible form, narrative films go to their own peer panel, and Artists of Colour are an OAC priority group. PURPLE's $47K budget is far under the $125K Emerging cap, and $10,000 would cover most of the post-production budget.
items.priorities: Supports Ontario media artists creating independent work in the production and post-production phases, where the director has creative and editorial control and holds copyright. Considers OAC's priority groups (including Artists of Colour) and strives for gender parity. Not intended for commercial media production.
items.eligibility: Ontario residents who are the director or principal media artist, working on their own initiative and holding copyright. Emerging: at least one completed independent media work you initiated as director (student work does not count) and not enrolled in a formal media arts program. Producers, and people who only contributed to others' projects, are not eligible.
items.watch_out: Matthew must already have at least one completed independent work he directed; being AD on Quiet Father does not count. The activity cannot start before results, which come about 4.5 months after the deadline (around early August 2027 for a March 2027 deadline), after the shoot has begun: frame the request around the Philippines shoot and post-production and confirm that framing with OAC first. The cheque is only released once all other revenue in the budget is confirmed, and the grant is forfeited if that is not done within a year. Excluded: producer-driven or 'calling-card' films, commissioned work, screenwriting, TV pilots. The 2027 dates were not yet published on 2026-11-16.
items.deadline: Two deadlines a year, 1 p.m. ET. The 2026 deadlines were 17 March and 8 October 2026; 2027 dates are not yet published. The form appears in Nova about two months before each deadline.
items.decision: About four and a half months after the deadline.

items.name: Ontario Film and Television Tax Credit (OFTTC)
items.amount: 35% of eligible Ontario labour (refundable, net of grants); 45% with the regional bonus; first-time production bonus of 40% on the first $240,000 of qualifying Ontario labour
items.why_fit: If PURPLE were produced by an Ontario corporation with a distribution deal and enough Ontario shooting days, about a third of its Ontario labour would come back, at a higher first-time rate.
items.priorities: Refundable tax credit for Ontario-based Canadian corporations producing Canadian film and television with Ontario labour.
items.eligibility: Canadian-controlled corporation with a permanent establishment in Ontario that files an Ontario tax return. The production needs 6 Canadian content points, at least 85% of principal photography days in Ontario, at least 95% of post-production costs in Ontario, at least 75% of total final costs spent in Ontario, and a written fair-market agreement to show it in Ontario within two years of completion.
items.watch_out: PURPLE fails several tests as planned: many shooting days are in Quebec, Alberta and the Philippines (the 85% Ontario-days rule only relaxes for interprovincial or treaty co-productions), there is no corporation, and there is no exhibition, broadcast or distribution agreement. Online-only releases also need a budget of at least $250,000. The credit is paid only after the corporate tax return is assessed, so it never helps cash flow during the shoot. Admin fee is 0.15% of estimated Ontario labour (minimum $500).
items.deadline: Apply any time from the start of principal photography until 24 months after the end of the corporation's taxation year in which principal photography began (extendable by 18 months with a CRA waiver).
items.how_to_apply: The production corporation applies for a Certificate of Eligibility on the Ontario Creates portal (during production or after completion), then for a Letter of Confirmation once the film is complete, and files the certificate with its T2 return and Schedule T2SCH556.

items.name: Quebec support for the Montreal shoot (SODEC, CALQ, Quebec production services tax credit)
items.funder: SODEC and Conseil des arts et des lettres du Québec
items.amount: Production services tax credit: 25% of qualified spending in Quebec
items.why_fit: Checked because PURPLE shoots in Montreal; none of it is open to PURPLE, so this entry saves the team the search.
items.priorities: SODEC and CALQ fund Quebec companies and Quebec-resident artists; the production services credit attracts outside productions to spend in Quebec.
items.eligibility: CALQ: Canadian citizens or permanent residents who normally live in Quebec and have done so for the past 12 months. SODEC emerging creation aid: a company registered in Quebec for at least a year (not a sole proprietorship) and a creator with at least two years of Quebec tax residence. Production services tax credit: a corporation with an establishment in Quebec whose main business is film or TV.
items.watch_out: PURPLE is shut out of all three. The production services tax credit is open to non-Quebec productions but needs a minimum budget of $250,000 (PURPLE is $47,335) and a corporation established in Quebec, and fees for the director, writer, DOP, editor, speaking actors and other key roles only count if those people live in Quebec. Montreal filming permits carry borough fees; the one schedule that mentions a waiver limits it to non-profit, TV news and student shoots.
items.tips: For the Montreal days, open a file with the Bureau du cinéma et de la télévision de Montréal before applying for any permit.

items.eligibility: Tax credit: a corporation incorporated or registered in Alberta, primarily in screen production, with total production costs of at least $499,999, a commercial distribution plan and 50% of financing secured. items.name: International Co-Production Fund (ICOF), minority co-production
items.funder: Film Development Council of the Philippines (Film Philippines Office)
items.amount: Feature, minority co-production: up to PHP 7 million (about CAD 160,000); majority: up to PHP 13 million. Cultural bonus of up to PHP 2 million with a passing cultural test. Non-recoupable, spent on Philippine costs through the Filipino co-producer.
items.why_fit: PURPLE's last act is a Filipino story shot in the Philippines with a local crew and Tagalog dialogue, which is what ICOF and its cultural bonus reward; with the local production company as minority co-producer, ICOF could pay for the whole Philippine shoot and some post.
items.priorities: A selective, non-recoupable grant to grow international co-productions between Filipino and foreign producers, with real Filipino creative and technical participation; a cultural bonus rewards projects that showcase Filipino culture.
items.eligibility: The applicant is a Filipino production company registered in the Philippines, active in the FDCP National Registry, with at least three publicly exhibited film or TV projects in the last five years, co-producing with an international production company. Minority track: the Filipino producer holds at least 10% of financing and the project has at least two Filipino above-the-line or three below-the-line key personnel. At least 60% of financing confirmed at application.
items.watch_out: PURPLE cannot apply itself: it needs a qualified Filipino company as co-producer (that company applies, receives the grant and must spend it in pesos through its own books), and the Canadian partner must be a production company, so a corporation is needed. 60% of the budget must be confirmed when applying. As far as this run could tell, Canada has no audiovisual co-production treaty with the Philippines, so this would be a private co-production agreement (check Telefilm's treaty list). Cycle dates are given by month only, and a cycle is cancelled if the year's budget runs out.
items.deadline: Two cycles a year: Cycle 1 applications in February (results in April), Cycle 2 applications in July (results in September). Exact 2027 dates are not yet published. Submissions via the FPO's online form on Philippine working days.
items.decision: Evaluation the month after the application month and announcement the month after that (about two months).
items.reopens: 2026 Cycle 2 opened at the end of July 2026 (FDCP notice dated 29 July 2026). Next expected Cycle 1 in February 2027, then Cycle 2 in July 2027.
items.closed_reason: No application cycle is open on the FDCP pages as of 2026-11-16.
items.how_to_apply: 1) Choose a Filipino production company with three exhibited credits and National Registry membership (ideally the one line-producing the September 2027 shoot) and sign a notarized co-production agreement giving it at least 10%. 2) The Filipino company submits through the FPO's online form: application form, co-production agreement, proof the Canadian co-producer can do business, letters from all confirmed financiers, script, project dossier, writer's agreement, pitch video, National Registry certificate and, optionally, the cultural test. All documents in English.
items.tips: Go for the cultural bonus: the Filipino family story, Tagalog dialogue and Philippine locations should score on the cultural test. A provisional application can be filed before, during or after principal photography, but only costs after the FPO receives a complete provisional notification count, so file before the September 2027 shoot. Post-production can be funded with a rough cut of at least 30 minutes.

items.name: Production Membership and Resource Access Network (member-rate gear in Toronto, Ottawa, Montreal, Calgary and Edmonton)
items.funder: LIFT (Liaison of Independent Filmmakers of Toronto) with the Independent Media Arts Alliance (IMAA)
items.amount: Member rental rates on cameras, lighting, grip, sound and post suites. Production membership $175 a year ($75 at the Equitable level for seniors and ODSP, Ontario Works or EI recipients). A 7-day rental is billed as 4 LIFT Days.
items.why_fit: PURPLE is an independent film under the director's creative control, the kind of project LIFT rents to. A LIFT Production membership also gets member rates at IMAA centres in the Canadian shoot cities on the route: DARC in Ottawa; MAIN FILM, Vidéographe and others in Montreal; CSIF in Calgary; FAVA in Edmonton. Renting locally at artist-run rates instead of from commercial houses could cut a real share of the $31,335 production budget. LIFT's editing, audio, colour and EasyDCP suites cover post.
items.priorities: LIFT supports independent filmmakers and does not rent to commercial or non-independent productions. The Resource Access Network lets members of one artist-run media centre use equipment and facilities in other cities without taking out multiple memberships.

Each RAN host decides what it offers, can refuse a request and sets its own insurance rules; some require your own production insurance. RAN guidelines say not to take a host's gear out of its region without asking, so rent in each city rather than hauling Toronto gear across provinces. Membership takes at least 10 business days to process, and Production applications sent after 4 Dec 2026 are processed from 6 Jan 2027. The Philippines leg is not covered.

Fill in the RAN booking form (services, dates, proof of membership signed by LIFT) and send it to the host at least 2 weeks before the rental.

Contact the production coordinators in Ottawa, Montreal, Calgary and Edmonton well before May 2027 to check what they stock and what insurance they need. LIFT does not require production insurance but encourages it.

items.name: Tax-receipted donations through a partner charity (intermediary arrangement)
items.funder: Canada Revenue Agency (rules for registered charities)
items.amount: Depends on donors; donors get official receipts only if a registered charity runs the activity
items.why_fit: The only Canadian way for PURPLE's larger donors to get a tax receipt: a registered charity whose purposes cover arts or culture (for example a Filipino-Canadian arts charity such as Kapisanan) runs a charitable activity linked to the film and uses the filmmaker as its intermediary under its direction and control.
items.priorities: CRA requires the charity to direct and control the activity and its money, ideally with a written agreement, regular reporting, money paid in instalments, and books kept in Canada. An intermediary can be an individual.
items.eligibility: Only a registered charity or other qualified donee can issue receipts. The filmmaker cannot issue them.
items.watch_out: Canada has no US-style 'fiscal sponsorship'. A charity that just passes donations through to a film is acting as a conduit and risks its registration, so most charities will say no unless the film clearly serves their charitable purpose (for example youth mentorship on set or community screenings). Gifts earmarked for one person, or that buy the donor credit or perks, may not be receiptable. CRA says sponsorship is not a gift. The newer 2023 rules that let charities make grants to non-qualified donees are for organizations, not individual artists. Get a charity lawyer or accountant to check the agreement. US fiscal sponsors (Film Independent, Fractured Atlas) give US receipts, not Canadian ones.
items.deadline: No deadline. Allow 2 to 3 months to find a charity, agree the activity and sign a written agreement before asking donors.
items.how_to_apply: Approach a registered arts or Filipino-Canadian cultural charity with a defined charitable activity tied to the film (mentorship of Filipino-Canadian youth on set, community screenings and workshops). Agree a written intermediary agreement, budget and reporting. Donations go to the charity, which receipts them and pays out in instalments.

items.eligibility: 'Your organization' or cause; run through Force4Good in Canada. The page does not say whether an individual artist's film project qualifies.

The money depends on turnout, probably hundreds rather than thousands of dollars, so the main value is visibility. There is no published route for food or cash sponsorship beyond this program. Jollibee Canada's own giving in 2026 went to charities (Make-A-Wish Canada, Boys and Girls Club).

items.name: Community partnership (Filipino-Canadian arts centre)

items.amount: In-kind: promotion, introductions, screening; the 48-Hour Film Challenge winner gets production support for a next film
items.why_fit: The Toronto non-profit behind Canada's Filipino film festival (at TIFF Lightbox). Its sponsor and media list is a ready map of who already pays for Filipino-Canadian film: TD, Kre8, Canada Film Equipment, Sony, Marquee Insurance, AV Communications, ABS-CBN, GMA Pinoy TV, OMNI and Filipino TV.
items.priorities: Nurturing Filipino talent in the creative industries through the festival, workshops, an Industry Conference and the 48-Hour Film Challenge.
items.eligibility: Filipino and Filipino-Canadian creators; calls go out on Instagram first.
items.watch_out: Siné looks for sponsors itself and is not a funder. A festival submission for PURPLE belongs on the competitions list. The 2027 festival is listed for April 2027 at TIFF Lightbox, before PURPLE is shot, so the useful slot is a work-in-progress or Industry Conference presence in 2027 and a screening in 2028.
items.deadline: Rolling for partnership talks. 48-Hour Film Challenge 6 to 7 March 2027; Industry Conference March 2027; festival April 2027.
items.how_to_apply: Email info@sineinstitute.com; follow @sineinstitute on Instagram for calls.
items.ask: Promotion of PURPLE's crowdfunding and casting to the Siné audience; introductions to its presenting partners and media partners (Canada Film Equipment, Kre8, TD, ABS-CBN, GMA Pinoy TV, OMNI); a work-in-progress pitch or talk at the March 2027 Industry Conference; a screening in 2028.
items.offer: Community partner credit, a Q&A and screening for Siné's audience, behind-the-scenes content for its channels, and mentorship or set visits for Siné workshop participants.

items.name: Corporate Sponsorships (sports and culture)
items.amount: Not published (in-kind travel or cash, in exchange for brand visibility)
items.why_fit: Air Canada flies Toronto-Calgary and has a published corporate sponsorship form that covers culture, and it already sponsors film festivals. Six return flights (about $4,200) is the ask.
items.priorities: Sports or culture with national or province-wide reach and mass appeal; tangible benefits (branded assets, activation space, hosting); engagement with attendees; exclusivity in the airline and vacation package category; an evaluation framework.
items.eligibility: Canadian organizations and properties that meet the criteria above. The Air Canada Foundation (grants and in-kind) is only for registered Canadian charities focused on children's and youth health. Community Relations and Partnerships is not accepting new requests.
items.watch_out: A first micro-budget feature with no distributor will struggle to show 'national reach' and 'mass appeal'; the realistic version comes after a festival selection. The Foundation route is for registered charities only. The community page footer says 2022, so confirm the forms are still live. No lead time is published for corporate sponsorships.
items.deadline: Rolling; no deadline published for corporate sponsorships. Send at least 3 months before the travel (the Foundation asks for 3 months for in-kind requests).
items.how_to_apply: Submit the Corporate Sponsorships form (Benevity). Only requests sent through the forms are considered.
items.ask: Six return Toronto-Calgary flights for the July 2027 Alberta shoot, or a discount code for cast and crew; later, travel for festival screenings.
items.offer: Exclusive 'official airline' credit in the end credits and on the poster, logo on the trailer and crowdfunding page, social posts, a tasteful in-film moment if it fits, and screening tickets.

items.name: Airport Community Giving (gift of flight)
items.amount: One round-trip flight for two to any WestJet destination, to be auctioned or raffled
items.why_fit: WestJet flies Toronto-Calgary, and a flight-for-two raffle prize could anchor a fundraising event for the film, but only if a charity or non-profit partner runs it.
items.priorities: In-kind support for charities, non-profits and community initiatives, reviewed by WestJetters at Canadian airports based on local needs.
items.eligibility: Charities and not-for-profit organizations, third-party requests supporting a charity or non-profit, and community events or initiatives.
items.watch_out: Excludes cash requests, sponsorship of fundraising or community events, and 'individuals raising money on their own'. The flight must be a raffle or packaged auction prize, not crew travel. PURPLE would need a non-profit partner (for example Kapisanan) to run the fundraiser for its own cause. No lead time is published.
items.deadline: Rolling; no lead time published. Apply at least 8 weeks before the fundraising event.
items.how_to_apply: The partner non-profit registers and submits the gift-of-flight request after reading WestJet's Giving Guidelines.
items.ask: A flight-for-two voucher as the main raffle prize at a partner non-profit's benefit screening or fundraiser.
items.offer: Thanks at the event and on the partner's channels; WestJet thanked in PURPLE's end credits if the event supports the film.

items.name: Community Support flight vouchers
items.amount: Free flight vouchers (amount not published)
items.why_fit: Toronto-based airline that gives free flight vouchers to causes that support community, foster diversity or raise awareness; a Filipino-Canadian story by racialized creators fits the diversity theme.
items.priorities: 'Free flight vouchers to help your cause soar, whether you are supporting your community, fostering diversity, or raising awareness.'
items.eligibility: Third-party listings say registered charities and non-profits in communities Porter serves.
items.watch_out: Porter's pages blocked automated reading, so the form's rules and lead time could not be confirmed. The program appears to be for charities and non-profits, so an individual film would need a non-profit partner. Vouchers are usually for raffles or charity travel, not crew flights.
items.deadline: Rolling; lead time not published. Apply at least 8 weeks ahead.
items.how_to_apply: Use 'Start application' in the Community Support section of Porter's Help & Contact page (https://www.flyporter.com/en-ca/customer-service/help-contact).
items.ask: Flight vouchers for a partner non-profit's fundraiser for the film, or for cast travel if the form allows it.
items.offer: End-credit thanks, logo on the crowdfunding page, social posts and screening tickets.

items.name: Film inquiries: filming in the Fossil Gallery and museum spaces
items.amount: Location access; fees not published (ask for a reduced rate)
items.why_fit: The museum's 'Dinosaur Hall' scene is in the script. The museum publishes a named contact for film and commercial shoots and says its castle building is a frequent backdrop for movies. Its theatre (with projector) is also rentable for a premiere screening in Ottawa.
items.priorities: The museum hosts photo and film shoots in its historic Ottawa building (a National Historic Site) and at its Natural Heritage Campus in Gatineau.
items.eligibility: Commercial, educational and media shoots by request.
items.watch_out: No fee schedule, small-production rate or waiver is published; expect a location fee, staff supervision, insurance and filming outside public hours. The dinosaur gallery is called the Fossil Gallery (horned dinosaurs). Ask early: the shoot is May to June 2027.
items.deadline: Rolling; no lead time published. Write by February 2027 for a May to June 2027 shoot.
items.how_to_apply: Email the film and commercial inquiries contact with the scene description, crew size (small), equipment, dates and the request for a reduced rate. For a screening, use the rentals inquiry form.
items.ask: Permission to film the father-and-son scene in the Fossil Gallery with a small crew outside public hours, at a reduced or waived location fee for a micro-budget Canadian feature; later, a discounted theatre rental for an Ottawa screening.
items.offer: End-credit thanks and location credit, stills and a short clip for the museum's channels, a screening and Q&A at the museum, and screening tickets for staff.

items.name: Filming permission and reduced location fee
items.funder: Notre-Dame Basilica of Montreal (Fabrique de la paroisse Notre-Dame de Montréal)
items.amount: Location access; no fees or waivers published
items.why_fit: The basilica is a named location in the script and is run by a non-profit Fabrique, which may grant a reduced rate to a small, respectful production.
items.priorities: A place of worship and heritage site with tourist visits and the AURA show.
items.eligibility: No filming policy is published.
items.watch_out: No filming rules, fees or small-production discount are published. The only published routes are the press request form and the general email (meant for media stories). Expect fees, filming outside masses, visits and AURA show times, and possibly a request to read the script. Filming the exterior from the street needs a City of Montreal permit through the Bureau du cinéma et de la télévision de Montréal.
items.deadline: Rolling; write by February 2027 for a May to June 2027 shoot.
items.how_to_apply: Write in French and English with the scene, crew size, dates and a respectful description of how the church is shown; ask who handles film shoots and their fees.
items.ask: Permission to film a short interior scene with a small crew outside public hours, at a reduced fee for a micro-budget feature.
items.offer: Location credit and thanks, a donation toward the restoration fund instead of a commercial fee, stills for their channels, and screening tickets.

items.name: Film permit or small-scale registration, Banff National Park (Lake Louise)
items.amount: No waiver. Crew of 1 to 6: $177.25 application fee per project plus $589.25 per filming day; small-scale registration where the project qualifies
items.why_fit: Needed for the July 2027 Banff and Lake Louise scenes; a crew of six or fewer keeps the fees at the lowest tier and may qualify for small-scale registration instead of a permit.
items.priorities: Small crews, low impact, public areas, no drones.
items.eligibility: Anyone filming commercially in the park; the application answers decide whether it is a Small-Scale Registration or a Commercial Film Permit.
items.watch_out: Major problem for the plan: commercial film projects are not considered at Lake Louise, Moraine Lake, Peyto Lake, Bow Lake, Johnston Canyon and other spots between 1 June and 30 September, which covers the July shoot. Ask the Banff Field Unit whether a small-scale registration is also blocked, or move those scenes to May or October, or use other locations. Lake Louise shoreline filming also needs the Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise's permission. Drones need extra permits. A business licence may be needed. Proof of liability insurance is usually required.
items.deadline: Rolling: submit at least 20 business days before filming (business licences take about 15 business days). Write by March 2027 to settle the summer restriction.
items.decision: Business licence service standard: 15 business days after a complete application.
items.how_to_apply: Fill in the Banff Film Permit / Temporary Business Licence form; for Lake Louise questions write to llykfilm@pc.gc.ca (published on the same page).
items.ask: Small-scale registration (or the lowest-tier permit) for a crew of six or fewer, and advice on which Lake Louise-area locations a narrative scene can use in July.
items.offer: Location credit and thanks to Parks Canada, and footage that shows respectful use of the park.

items.name: Commercial film permit or small-scale registration, Jasper National Park (Dark Sky Preserve)
items.amount: Small-scale registration is free but only for small travel-focused projects; otherwise crew of 1 to 6: $177.25 application plus $589.25 per day, plus park entry
items.why_fit: Needed for the Jasper Dark Sky Preserve night scenes in July 2027. A crew of six or fewer keeps costs at the lowest tier.
items.priorities: Off-season and weekday shoots are prioritized. Small-scale registration requires that the project 'informs the public about Parks Canada and promotes authentic, realistic experiences'.
items.eligibility: Small-scale registration: six people or fewer including talent, hand-held equipment, public areas only, no drones, travel focus. Everything else needs a commercial permit.
items.watch_out: A narrative feature probably does not count as a 'travel focus' project, so expect the commercial permit and fees. Night filming outside normal hours ('off-hours access') needs a commercial permit. Jasper is only taking commercial applications for projects before 1 April 2027 (page modified 2026-11-03), so the July 2027 application cannot be made yet. Permits do not cover park entry fees.
items.deadline: Submit at least 20 business days before filming once Jasper opens applications for projects after 1 April 2027.
items.reopens: Not announced. Check the page in early 2027 and write to the Jasper film contact to ask when July 2027 projects can apply.
items.closed_reason: Jasper is only accepting commercial film applications for projects happening before 1 April 2027.
items.how_to_apply: Ask the Jasper film contact whether PURPLE's small crew can use small-scale registration; if not, send the commercial application Word form with insurance details when applications open.
items.ask: Small-scale registration or the lowest-tier permit for a crew of six, permission for night filming in the Dark Sky Preserve, and advice on low-light locations.
items.offer: Location credit and thanks to Parks Canada; night-sky footage that promotes the Dark Sky Preserve.

items.name: Media team filming support (b-roll library and leaseholder contacts)
items.amount: In-kind: HD b-roll library, itinerary help, introductions to leaseholders and local experts
items.why_fit: Its b-roll library could supply establishing shots of Lake Louise and Moraine Lake that PURPLE cannot film itself in July because of Parks Canada's summer restriction, and its team can contact leaseholders such as the Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise.
items.priorities: Content that promotes Banff and Lake Louise as a travel destination; media visit support favours confirmed assignments tied to its pillars (soft adventure, culinary, wellness, sustainability, events).
items.eligibility: Media and productions filming in Banff and Lake Louise.
items.watch_out: It does not issue permits or pay for lodging for films, and its media-visit support is aimed at travel media with a confirmed outlet, so a feature may get only b-roll and contacts. Check the licence terms for using b-roll in a feature film. Lake Louise filming needs both Parks Canada and Fairmont permission.
items.deadline: Rolling; the media visit form asks for at least three weeks' notice. Write by March 2027.
items.how_to_apply: Email the media team with the shoot dates, locations, crew size and the b-roll you need.
items.ask: Licence to use HD b-roll of Lake Louise and Moraine Lake in the film; help contacting leaseholders (Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise) and choosing locations open to filming in July.
items.offer: End-credit thanks and destination credit, behind-the-scenes clips and stills of the shoot for their channels, and screening tickets.

items.name: Tourism Jasper and Jasper Dark Sky Festival partnership
items.amount: In-kind (contacts, promotion, a possible screening); no sponsorship program published
items.why_fit: PURPLE's night scenes in the Jasper Dark Sky Preserve match the festival Tourism Jasper runs every October; a 2028 screening at the festival would be a natural fit.
items.priorities: Promoting Jasper and the world's largest accessible Dark Sky Preserve; the 2026 festival ran 14 to 26 October.
items.eligibility: General inquiries; the festival also runs a call for speakers.
items.watch_out: No sponsorship or film-support program is published; the only route is the general inquiry email. Jasper is still rebuilding after the 2024 wildfire. 2027 festival dates are not posted yet.
items.deadline: Rolling; write by April 2027 for the July 2027 shoot.
items.how_to_apply: Email with the shoot dates, the Dark Sky scenes and the request.
items.ask: Introductions to local astronomers or night-sky guides and to lodging partners who may give a film rate; later, a screening of PURPLE at the Dark Sky Festival in October 2028.
items.offer: End-credit thanks, night-sky clips and stills for Tourism Jasper's channels, and a festival screening with Q&A.

items.name: Free City of Ottawa filming permits and Ottawa Film Office location help
items.funder: Ottawa Film Office and City of Ottawa (Event Central)
items.amount: City filming permits are free; fees apply only for on-street parking, park rentals, municipal facilities, late applications ($200) and Traffic Management approval ($200)
items.why_fit: The Ottawa scenes (May to June 2027) can be permitted at no cost on City property, and the Film Office helps connect productions with locations, crew and the federal bodies that control places like Parliament Hill.
items.priorities: Attracting productions to Ottawa; the Film Office gives location support and advice.
items.eligibility: Any production filming on City property.
items.watch_out: Parliament Hill is federal property, not City property, so it needs separate federal permission; ask the Film Office who to contact. An insurance certificate and indemnity for the City are required. Free permits save money but bring no cash.
items.deadline: Rolling: apply to Event Central at least 5 business days before filming (longer for road closures or paid duty officers). Contact the Film Office by March 2027 about Parliament Hill.
items.how_to_apply: Contact the Ottawa Film Office through its form (phone 613-695-1955) for location help; apply for City permits through Event Central using the forms on ottawa.ca.
items.ask: Location advice, introductions for Parliament Hill and federal sites, and free City permits for street scenes.
items.offer: End-credit thanks to the Ottawa Film Office and City of Ottawa, and stills for the Film Office's channels.

items.name: Production Program: English-language window for budgets under $3.5M
items.why_fit: PURPLE's $47,335 budget sits far under the $3.5M line, and this is Telefilm's regular feature-film production window for English-language projects; a Canadian company with PURPLE as its project could use it after Talent to Watch.
items.watch_out: Applicants must be Canadian audiovisual production companies with a head office in Canada, so PURPLE needs a corporation first. Only one submission per fiscal year. Decision around mid-June 2027 comes after the May 2027 shoot starts, so it fits post-production or a later phase better. Telefilm's page gave no amounts or a distributor rule; read the Guidelines and Essential Information Guide.
items.deadline: Window opens 26 Jan 2027, 8:00am EST and closes 9 Feb 2027, 11:59pm EST (English, budgets under $3.5M).
items.decision: About mid-June 2027.
items.reopens: Telefilm runs several windows a year; the next English under-$3.5M window after this one is not published yet.
items.how_to_apply: The applicant company applies through Telefilm's online portal, Dialogue, while the window is open. Register the company and read the Guidelines and Essential Information Guide first.
items.tips: Telefilm's page says projects in languages other than English or French use the English low-budget window; PURPLE's Tagalog and French dialogue should be checked against the language rules.

items.name: Filming permit and BCTM file (fee waivers for non-profit and student shoots)
items.funder: Bureau du cinéma et de la télévision de Montréal (City of Montréal)
items.why_fit: PURPLE shoots in Montreal in May to June 2027 (Notre-Dame Basilica, street and road-trip scenes); a permit is needed for any public-property filming, and costs are low.
items.watch_out: Fees are small ($30 permit plus daily occupancy), and the page's 'no charge for non-profit, television news and student shoots' appears in one borough's section, so PURPLE may not qualify. Needs $1M to $5M third-party liability insurance naming the City as co-insured. Application form is in French. A separate application is needed for each public place.
items.deadline: Rolling. Apply at least 10 to 15 business days before filming (14 in some boroughs).
items.reopens: Always open.
items.how_to_apply: Contact the BCTM first to open a file and get a file number, then complete the online application for each public place. Permits are valid up to one month.

items.name: Partnerships and sponsorships program (train tickets)
items.why_fit: PURPLE is a road trip across Canada; VIA Rail has given film-related help as train tickets, in exchange for visibility.
items.watch_out: VIA Rail's own page says it has paused its partnerships and sponsorships program, so nothing can be requested now. It limits help to Canadian initiatives, has given tickets rather than cash, and expects equal-value visibility in return (from third-party reports).
items.deadline: Program paused; no way to apply.
items.reopens: No date given. Re-check each quarter.
items.closed_reason: VIA Rail states on its sponsorship page that it has paused its partnerships and sponsorships program.
items.ask: Train tickets for cast and crew on a Toronto to Ottawa or Montreal leg.
items.offer: End-credit thanks, logo on the poster, a thank-you social post and screening invitations.
